item.title: The Jack Daniel’s Age-Stated Releases Are a Hit, but How Old Can the Tennessee Whiskey Get?
item.description: When it comes to high-end whiskey, Jack Daniel’s is on a roll. (Or perhaps more appropriately, a heater, based on the ABV of some high-octane releases.) From toasted barrel whiskey to “hazmat” rye, the famed Tennessee distillery has staked its claim among top producers of premium spirits. Those efforts have helped expand the brand beyond the Old No. 7 bottle, an omnipresent SKU that keeps it among the top two biggest sellers of American whiskey. item.title: The World’s Best Riesling Regions, Mapped
item.description: Riesling is a profoundly aromatic grape used to create several distinct styles of wine. It’s also one of the most popular white wine grapes in the world. Native to Germany, the grape is exceptionally durable, with relatively thick skin that allows it to thrive in cool climates and develop its signature acidity. item.title: Ask a Somm: Does Wine Really Need to Rest After Traveling?
item.description: While some drinkers purchase their wine at bars, restaurants, and liquor stores, others anxiously await the arrival of a case at their doorsteps. Tourists order bottles to their homes after traveling to winemaking regions, wine clubs ship cases to subscribers, and another sector of consumers purchase theirs from the vineyards themselves. item.title: The VinePair Podcast: The Opportunities for American Wine – LIVE
item.description: It seems that each day brings a new headline about younger generations’ drinking slump, but the doom and gloom offers American wine the opportunity to reinvent its old ways to meet the desires of contemporary drinkers. Now is a pivotal time for the U.S. wine scene, but it’s up to the producers to speak with consumers and adapt to their changing demands. item.title: 6 of the Best Soave Wines From Italy’s Veneto
item.description: Soave, the large and once easily dismissed appellation in Italy’s northeast Veneto region, produces some of Italy’s most exciting white wines. Actually, it always has, but was overshadowed by industrial-scale winemaking that took root in the 1970s and ’80s as the Soave zone was greatly expanded. Soave became synonymous with cheap, insipid, industrial wines — the white-wine companion to the red Valpolicella, also from the Veneto. item.title: You’ve Heard of West Coast IPAs, but What Is a West Coast Pilsner?
item.description: The India pale ale (IPA) is easily the world’s most popular beer style, skyrocketing to the top of the craft beer canon in the late 20th century. By the mid-2010s, the style was virtually inescapable in taprooms and bottle shops, with offerings dominated by the New England (or hazy) IPA subcategory.
